channels.title: Channels
channels.description: A channel is a handoff point, with optional room for stored values. Compare a direct meeting with a small waiting shelf before closing the path.
channels.html:
A channel is a handoff point, with optional room for stored values. Compare a direct meeting with a small waiting shelf before closing the path.

  • Say how many values make(chan int, 2) can hold before a send waits
  • Explain why a closed channel still hands out its buffered values
  • Use v, ok := <-ch to tell a sent value from a closed, empty channel

select.title: Select
select.description: Select is listening at several doors at once. Make more than one door ready and try another seed before assuming one case always wins.
select.html:
Select is listening at several doors at once. Make more than one door ready and try another seed before assuming one case always wins.

  • Say what select does when two cases are ready at once
  • Explain why the order of cases in the code is not a priority
  • Make the choice certain by leaving only one case ready

synchronization.title: Synchronization
synchronization.description: A mutex is a key for a shared notebook. Give each worker the key before its update and wait until all workers put their pencils down.
synchronization.html:
A mutex is a key for a shared notebook. Give each worker the key before its update and wait until all workers put their pencils down.

  • Say what job the mutex does and what job the WaitGroup does
  • Explain why count++ must happen between Lock and Unlock
  • Predict the count when more goroutines join in

ordering-and-the-memory-model.title: Ordering and the memory model
ordering-and-the-memory-model.description: A happens-before edge is a receipt proving one event came before another. Look for a receipt rather than treating one animation’s order as a guarantee.
ordering-and-the-memory-model.html:
A happens-before edge is a receipt proving one event came before another. Look for a receipt rather than treating one animation’s order as a guarantee.

  • Point to the two goroutines that write x with nothing ordering them
  • Explain why getting 2 on one run does not prove the code is safe
  • Add a mutex so the writes happen one at a time

pipelines.title: Pipelines
pipelines.description: A pipeline is a line of workstations passing parcels onward. Close the handoff when a stage is finished, and watch what happens when a downstream station…
pipelines.html:
A pipeline is a line of workstations passing parcels onward. Close the handoff when a stage is finished, and watch what happens when a downstream station leaves early.

  • Trace one value from the first stage to the printout
  • Say who closes each channel, and why it is the sender
  • Explain how range over a channel knows when to stop

cancellation.title: Cancellation
cancellation.description: Cancellation is a stop message sent down a family tree. Let each worker listen and leave its station instead of assuming someone can forcibly erase it.
cancellation.html:
Cancellation is a stop message sent down a family tree. Let each worker listen and leave its station instead of assuming someone can forcibly erase it.

  • Say what cancel() actually does to ctx.Done()
  • Explain why the worker only stops because it listens on Done()
  • Read ctx.Err() to learn why a context ended

concurrency-bug-clinic.title: Concurrency bug clinic
concurrency-bug-clinic.description: Debugging concurrency is finding a broken traffic rule, not guessing the fastest car. Inspect blocked tasks and conflicting accesses, then change the rule…
concurrency-bug-clinic.html:
Debugging concurrency is finding a broken traffic rule, not guessing the fastest car. Inspect blocked tasks and conflicting accesses, then change the rule and rerun the check.

  • Say why wg.Add(1) comes before the go line
  • Explain how defer wg.Done() covers every way out of the goroutine
  • Predict what happens if Add and the number of goroutines disagree
